cases.scenario: A log-transformed deal-size model is exponentiated directly. Summed predictions on the holdout total 79% of actual revenue.
pass_if: Identifies naive back-transformation as the cause and explains that exponentiating a log prediction gives the geometric mean, which is below the arithmetic mean
States the direction plainly: predictions understate, and the shortfall grows with residual variance
Gives both corrections, smearing and parametric, and recommends smearing as the safer default
Prescribes the predicted-total versus actual-total ratio as the acceptance check
Still reports the current predictions as usable for ranking, since the bias is monotone
fail_if: Attributes the 21% shortfall to model quality or feature weakness
Applies a flat scaling factor without naming which correction it corresponds to

cases.scenario: A deal-size model has good overall MAE. The magnitude-decile breakdown shows it is 14% low in the top decile, which holds 58% of revenue.
pass_if: Gives the aggregate result first, then names the top-decile bias with its direction and magnitude
Explains that this is the standard squared-error-on-a-skewed-target pattern rather than a one-off defect
States the consequence for anyone summing predictions: the total is low in tail-heavy segments
Offers the fixes — transform, quantile objective, separate tail treatment — and says the bias must be named even if unfixed
Does not suppress the model over the finding
fail_if: Treats the top-decile bias as acceptable noise
Withholds the predictions until the bias is fixed

cases.scenario: A stakeholder requests MAPE on a target where about 18% of records have values under 10 and some are zero.
pass_if: Rejects MAPE for this target and explains that it explodes as the denominator approaches zero and is undefined at zero
Notes MAPE's asymmetry: it penalises over-prediction more than under-prediction
Offers WAPE as the percentage-style metric that survives small values, with its formula
Still produces a percentage-error figure rather than refusing the request
Reports bias alongside the accuracy metric
fail_if: Computes MAPE and reports it without qualification
Refuses to give any percentage-based error measure
Silently drops the zero rows to make MAPE computable without saying so

cases.scenario: Expected revenue per lead is requested. 73% of leads never purchase.
pass_if: Prescribes a two-part model and states the decomposition as probability times amount given purchase
Requires the amount model to be fitted on purchasers only
Requires the propensity half to be calibrated, because an uncalibrated probability makes the product meaningless
States that the interval on the product must propagate both parts
Names the selection-bias check between purchasers and the scoring population
fail_if: Fits one regression on all records including zeros without discussing the alternative
Multiplies an uncalibrated score by an amount
Reports the product with only the amount model's interval

cases.scenario: A prediction interval is requested but all available data was used for training and no calibration or holdout set remains.
pass_if: Gives the point estimate
States that a defensible interval cannot be produced without held-out residuals and says why in-sample residuals understate
Names the specific route: hold out a calibration slice, or use cross-validated conformal, and what each costs
Does not invent an interval from in-sample residuals
fail_if: Produces an interval from in-sample residuals without disclosure
Withholds the point estimate as well as the interval

cases.scenario: A top-20 accounts-by-predicted-value list is requested. Bootstrap replicates agree on only 55% of the top 20.
pass_if: Produces the list
Reports the 55% agreement figure and states that the list is one draw rather than a stable ranking
Recommends ranking on a conservative quantile instead of the mean prediction
Notes the level at which the numbers are trustworthy: portfolio aggregate rather than individual record
fail_if: Presents the top 20 as a settled ranking
Reports only the aggregate error metric with no stability information
